title: 7-trial RAWM protocol
author: Teresa Macheda
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bb84iryw
materials: RAWM apparatus (circular platform, base, 8-shaped platform, 8 metal inserts, escape platform)
Spatial cues (triangle, square, checkboard pattern, cross)

steps.title: Assign Codes and Randomize Order
steps.instruction: Code each experimental group so the operator is blinded, and randomize the order in which individual mice will be tested to avoid group‑order bias.

steps.title: Assemble and Prepare RAWM Apparatus
steps.instruction: Isolate the maze with double black‑out curtains; set light intensity to 4‑6 lux in each arm and the centre. Assemble the circular pool (diameter 121 cm, depth 75 cm) by placing the 9‑cm base, the 8‑shaped platform, and eight metal inserts (65 cm × 42 cm) to form an 8‑arm maze. Number the inserts for consistent arm orientation. Add liquid paint, fill with water, and raise the arms 9 cm above the water surface. Position the 8‑cm‑diameter escape platform (57 cm high) 1 cm below the water surface. Place four extra‑maze cues (triangle, square, checkerboard, cross) made of white corrugated plastic and black vinyl around the maze and keep them constant. Keep a 16‑cm tall flag ready to make the platform visible when required.

steps.title: Handle Mice and Pre‑test Checks
steps.instruction: Handle each mouse for at least three consecutive days and mark the tail for identification. One or two days before testing, inspect the pool for damage or leaks and verify that the overhead lights function correctly.

steps.title: Prepare Recovery Cages and Heating Pads
steps.instruction: Set up clean recovery cages with paper towels; place only half of each cage on a heating pad so the mouse can self‑regulate temperature. Replace wet paper towels promptly during the experiment.

steps.title: Acclimate Mice in Testing Room
steps.instruction: Move the home cages to the testing room and transfer each mouse to a clean, bedding‑free recovery cage for at least 30 minutes before the first trial.

steps.title: Verify Pool Temperature and Lighting
steps.instruction: Measure the pool water temperature and confirm it is 21 ± 1 °C. Verify that the light level in each arm and the centre is 4‑6 lux before starting any trial.

steps.title: Run Block 1 Trials (Trials 1‑3)
steps.instruction: Test the first cohort (10‑15 mice) then the second cohort using the following sequence, allowing 10‑15 minutes between trials for the same mouse and 50‑60 minutes between blocks.

substeps.instruction: Trial 1 (visible platform): Place the 16‑cm flag on the platform, gently place the mouse into the designated start arm facing the pool wall, and allow up to 60 s to locate the platform. The tracking software records latency, distance, speed and errors (incorrect arm entry or entry into the goal arm without escape). If the mouse spends >15 s in one location, record an additional error. If the mouse has not found the platform after 60 s, guide it gently to the platform. Allow the mouse to remain on the platform for 15 s, then remove, dry, and return it to its recovery cage.

Trial 2 (hidden platform): After all mice in the cohort have completed Trial 1, remove the flag so the platform is hidden. Repeat the actions of Trial 1 (placement, 60 s limit, data recording, 15‑s stay on platform) using a different semi‑random drop arm.
Trial 3 (visible platform): Replace the flag to make the platform visible again. Repeat the actions of Trial 1 with a new drop arm.

steps.title: Run Block 2 Trials (Trials 4‑7)
steps.instruction: After a 50‑60 minute interval, test the same cohort with four consecutive hidden‑platform trials, then repeat the block with the second cohort.

substeps.instruction: Trial 4 (hidden platform): Ensure the platform remains hidden (no flag). Follow the same placement, 60 s limit, data capture, and 15‑s platform stay as in Trial 2.
Trial 5 (hidden platform): Repeat the procedure with a new semi‑random drop arm.
Trial 6 (hidden platform): Repeat the procedure with a new semi‑random drop arm.
Trial 7 (hidden platform): Repeat the procedure with a new semi‑random drop arm.

steps.title: Dry Mice and Return to Home Cage
steps.instruction: After each trial, gently dry the mouse with paper towels before placing it back into its recovery cage; after the final trial of the day, allow the mouse to dry completely and then return it to its home cage. If a cohort contains fewer than 10 mice, increase the resting time between blocks accordingly.

steps.title: Conduct Testing Days (All Hidden)
steps.instruction: On Days 3 and 4 repeat the entire sequence of Block 1 (Trials 1‑3) and Block 2 (Trials 4‑7) for each cohort, but keep the platform hidden for every trial (no flag). Follow the same inter‑trial (10‑15 min) and inter‑block (50‑60 min) intervals, and apply the same drying and data‑recording procedures.

steps.title: Record Data and Score Errors
steps.instruction: Use the chosen tracking software to record latency, distance travelled, speed, and number of errors for each mouse. Score an error when the mouse enters a non‑goal arm, enters the goal arm without escaping, or remains ≥10 s in the same arm or centre (operator may also note >15 s stationary as an error).

steps.title: Clean and Disinfect Pool
steps.instruction: The day before testing, inspect the pool and stir the water to ensure even paint opacity. After the final experiment, empty the pool, rinse with clean water, then clean with a disinfecting solution. Wash and disinfect all arms and the platform before storage.
